claims.text: Particle size is the dominant factor governing premelting and melting behavior in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Smaller particles have a higher surface-to-volume ratio than larger particles.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio enhances atomic mobility at the particle surface.
Enhanced surface mobility reduces the energy barrier for initiating surface disorder.
Enhanced surface mobility lowers the melting point of smaller particles relative to larger particles.
Smaller particles contain a larger proportion of atoms at or near the surface.
Surface atoms have different bonding environments and lower coordination numbers than interior atoms.
Reduced coordination enhances the mobility of surface atoms.
Enhanced surface-atom mobility causes surface premelting to begin at a lower temperature.
Earlier surface premelting destabilizes the particle interior and lowers the energy barrier for complete melting.
Smaller Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles will exhibit lower premelting-onset temperatures than larger nanoparticles.
Smaller Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles will exhibit lower complete-melting temperatures than larger nanoparticles.
The temperature gap between premelting and complete melting will be larger in smaller particles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles around 100 nm exhibit bulk-like melting with minimal premelting effects.
The proposed size-dependent mechanism is expected to apply from approximately 5 nm to 100 nm under moderate heating rates.
Extreme particle sizes or highly nonlinear heating conditions may introduce effects outside the proposed model.
The magnitude of the premelting- and melting-temperature reductions depends on simulation details and heating rate.
Surface compositional and microstructural variations may complicate the observed melting behavior.
